lens:benchmark.summary:
BENCHMARK lens: I checked Nexdata's DatasetSpec (app/catalog/spec.py:45-74) against Snowflake Marketplace, Databricks Marketplace and Unity Catalog, AWS Data Exchange, DataHub, OpenMetadata, Kaggle's usability score, Datasheets for Datasets, schema.org Dataset / Google Dataset Search and DCAT-US v1.1. The live DB was reachable. All numbers below come from get_catalog() and information_schema, run read-only.

**Where Nexdata is already ahead.** The rights and governance fields are more structured than any marketplace listing: license, redistribution plus effective_redistribution, pii_class, origin, reviewed, rerun policy, slo_lag_hours and grain (spec.py:52-62, 72). Snowflake, Databricks and AWS keep most of this in free-text legal terms. status_public (ga/beta/internal/archival/retired) does the same job as Unity Catalog's certified/deprecated system tags and DataHub's status/deprecation. `inputs` is a first step toward DataHub-style upstreamLineage.

**What every benchmark has that Nexdata lacks or leaves empty:**
1. **Column-level data dictionary.** Snowflake data dictionary, AWS dataset schemas and DDQ, Kaggle column descriptions, DataHub schemaMetadata, DCAT describedBy. The catalog carries no columns at all. Only 2 of 7,743 columns in the public and core schemas have a COMMENT, and 39 of 478 tables.
2. **Short subtitle plus keywords, tags or categories.** Snowflake subtitle and business needs, Databricks short description (under 100 chars) and categories, AWS short description and up to 2 categories, Kaggle subtitle and tags, DCAT keyword (required), schema.org keywords. Nexdata has neither. The median description is 77 chars, and 6 of 150 are under Google's 50-char minimum.
3. **Temporal and spatial coverage.** Databricks time range and geographic coverage, schema.org temporalCoverage and spatialCoverage, DCAT temporal and spatial. coverage_from is set on 0 of 150 datasets and coverage_sql on 11 of 150. There is no geography field.
4. **A named contact or owner.** DCAT contactPoint is required and AWS requires a support contact. owner is 'data-platform' on all 150 datasets.
5. **A license URL.** Google wants an unambiguous, version-specific license URL, and DCAT's license field is a URL. Nexdata's license is free text; 27 datasets say 'Mixed: mostly US federal…'.
6. **Samples and quick-start queries.** Snowflake quick-start SQL and notebooks, Databricks up to 10 sample notebooks, AWS sample files and trial listings, Kaggle public notebooks. Nexdata has none.
7. **Version and release.** schema.org version and DCAT modified. Nexdata has none; this is only planned in the SPEC_130 envelope.
8. **Methodology and known limitations.** Datasheets 'collection process' and 'preprocessing', AWS DDQ, schema.org measurementTechnique. Only 6 datasets have notes.
9. **Primary key.** AWS explicitly asks for the primary key. It is set on 8 of 150; sec_form_d and sec_13f have none.

**Minimal set for a B2B DaaS selling PE and entity data.** Scope it to about 20 PE and entity datasets, not all 150. Add subtitle, keywords, temporal_coverage (coverage_from plus coverage_sql), spatial_coverage, license_url, contact, schema_version, a methodology/limitations text, a generated column dictionary, one sample query each, and a flag for whether personal data is available only from public sources (for AWS's 4-way sensitive-information declaration). Nothing here is a blocker for selling. The real blocker is that reviewed=True on 0 datasets, so effective_redistribution is internal_only everywhere and nothing is sellable yet.

**JSON-LD.** Build a pure to_jsonld() mapper now (cheap, and it doubles as a contract test that the metadata is complete). Emit it on public pages only once a public landing page exists and at least one dataset is ga/beta with a reviewed rights block. Use schema.org Dataset with isAccessibleForFree=false, and optionally DCAT (W3C DCAT, not DCAT-US: the US profile's bureauCode and programCode are federal-only fields). Don't publish SEO markup for internal or archival datasets.

**Cheap gaps** (dataclass fields plus data entry for about 20 datasets): subtitle, keywords, spatial_coverage, coverage_from, license_url, contact, schema_version, primary_key and coverage_sql on the flagships. **Medium:** column dictionary with descriptions (column names and types come free from information_schema; writing the descriptions is the work), a sample-rows endpoint gated on redistribution, and methodology write-ups.

lens:discovery.summary:
The catalog is well built for operators, but people can't yet use it to find data. Here is what exists. `GET /catalog` has no response model, and its `q` filter is a plain substring match over key, name and description (app/catalog/registry.py:238). `GET /catalog/{key}` makes up to 12 exact count(*) calls under a 20 s deadline (live.py:34-38), which is too slow for a browsing page. No frontend page renders the catalog. status.html (the ops status page) fetches /api/v1/catalog only to enrich its operator table (status.html:531).

The metadata that product pages need is mostly missing or inconsistent. None of the 150 specs has coverage_from. 8 have primary_key, 10 have inputs and 8 have upstream_url. All 150 have owner set to "data-platform". Descriptions have a median length of 77 characters. The live DB has only 2 column comments, and 20 of the 195 declared tables don't exist. No dataset is ga or beta, so the "Public" view the DaaS review recommends would be empty today.

Much of the missing structure can be derived without hand-writing it:
- 81 of the 85 datasets whose first table uses a surrogate `id` key have a unique index that gives the natural key.
- Shared identifier columns link the datasets into a real graph: cik appears in 18 catalog tables, crd_number in 10, crd in 3, naics_code in 6, county_fips in 5, zip_code in 9 and zip in 2. The naming is inconsistent (crd vs crd_number, zip vs zip_code), so the related-datasets feature needs a small alias map.
- The 175 existing declared tables have 3,242 columns in total, small enough for an in-memory search index.

The existing pieces for a "sample" and "how to access" section don't fit the catalog. The export preview is admin-only (SPEC_127). It only covers the public schema (export.py:208), so it misses the core.* entity tables. It runs an unbounded COUNT(*) (export.py:222), which is slow on the 3.8M-row sec_13f_holdings table. It also ignores rights and PII.

Proposal: one static, no-build page, frontend/catalog.html, in the same style as status.html (its CSS tokens, auth.js, esc(), and a pure helper block that node tests can run). It would have:
- a facet rail for kind, source, status, rights, PII, origin, cadence and freshness
- ranked search
- a hash-routed detail page (`#/d/{key}`). nginx's `try_files … /index.html` rewrites unknown paths, so path routing won't work.
- product pages for the PE/entity pack

Behind it, four small, cheap endpoints: `/catalog/facets`, a ranked `/catalog/search`, `/catalog/{key}/schema` and `/catalog/{key}/sample`. It also needs response models, a status join for freshness, reverse lineage and a derived identifier graph. Findings came from reading the code plus live read-only DB queries (information_schema, pg_index, pg_class estimates); Docker responded normally.

recommendations.title: Build frontend/catalog.html: faceted browser plus hash-routed dataset detail, in the status.html conventions
recommendations.detail:
One static file, no build step. Load /js/auth.js (SPEC_127 bearer wrapper and 401 redirect). Copy the :root tokens and card, header and nav-link classes from status.html:13-80, and put a pure `<script id="catalog-core">` helper block (filtering, ranking, facet counts, freshness bucketing, esc) under node tests the way tests/test_spec_125 exercises status-core. Layout:
(1) A header with nav links: Console, Status, Catalog. Add a 'Catalog ->' tab link next to the Status link at index.html:2042.
(2) A left facet rail with counts per value: kind, source (54 values), status_public, effective_redistribution, pii_class, origin, cadence, and a freshness bucket (current / behind / stalled / dormant / never_run, taken from GET /datasets/status).
(3) Result cards showing display_name, key, a one-line description, grain, badges (kind, rights, PII, origin), rows_total, coverage_through and a freshness dot.
(4) A detail route at `catalog.html#/d/{key}`. Hash routing is needed because nginx `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html` (frontend/nginx.conf:9) would swallow /catalog/{key}.
Detail sections: Overview (description, grain, cadence, owner, upstream link); Coverage and freshness (coverage_from to coverage_through, lag against the SLO, last success, next run, from the status API); Schema (the columns endpoint); Sample (the sample endpoint); Lineage (inputs upstream, reverse inputs downstream, producer); Rights (license, attribution text with a copy button, redistribution vs effective, PII, reviewed flag); How to access (curated endpoints, export, a curl snippet); Related datasets (shared identifiers).
Keep facet state in the URL (`#/?kind=entity&rights=open`) so views can be shared. Default to 'Show all (internal preview)', because 0 of 150 specs are ga or beta. A public-only toggle like status.html:281-282 would render empty today.

recommendations.title: Add GET /catalog/facets and a ranked GET /catalog/search, and give every catalog route a response_model
recommendations.detail:
Today filter_specs (app/catalog/registry.py:220-241) matches only one lower-cased substring against key, display_name and description, returns results in declaration order, and has no pii, origin or cadence filters. The API routes (app/api/v1/catalog.py:276, 297) have no response_model, so OpenAPI shows no schema.
Build an in-memory index at import time: 150 specs, plus 3,242 columns across 175 existing tables, loaded lazily from information_schema and cached with the catalog TTL. Postgres full-text search isn't needed at this size. The search should:
- tokenise the query (AND across tokens, prefix match)
- weight fields: key and display_name 5, table names 3, column names 2, grain / description / source / attribution / notes 1
- return `{key, score, matched:[field...], highlight}`
- accept multi-value filters: kind, source, status_public, redistribution, effective_redistribution, pii_class, origin, cadence, has_coverage
- sort by relevance, name, rows or freshness
`GET /catalog/facets` returns counts per facet value for the current filter set, so the rail can show 'entity (7)'.
Add Pydantic models `CatalogEntry`, `CatalogList`, `CatalogDetail`, `LiveStats` and `Rights`, with field descriptions copied from the comments in spec.py:47-74, plus `summary=` and examples. The catalog is then self-documenting in /docs, and a later client can be generated from it.
recommendations.evidence: app/catalog/registry.py:220-241; app/api/v1/catalog.py:276-316 (no response_model, no summary); app/catalog/spec.py:47-74; live: 3,242 columns in 175 of 195 declared tables

recommendations.title: Add GET /catalog/{key}/schema: a column dictionary from information_schema plus a curated overlay
recommendations.detail:
Schema is the main thing missing from a consumer detail page. Only 2 column comments exist in public and core (pg_description with objsubid > 0), and 39 table comments.
Return, per resolved table (reuse live.resolve_tables, so the core.* schemas are included): column name, data_type, nullable, pk / unique-index membership, the comment if one exists, an `identifier` tag (see the related-datasets recommendation), and a `pii` tag. Order the output as the declared table order, then ordinal position.
Add an optional `columns: Mapping[str, str]` description overlay to DatasetSpec, starting with the 11 PE/entity-pack datasets. This is the SPEC_137 column-dictionary item from the DaaS review, pulled forward because the catalog page needs it before Alembic `COMMENT ON` generation lands.
For tables that are declared but missing (20 of 195 today), return exists:false. The UI then shows 'declared, not yet built' instead of an error.
recommendations.evidence: docs/reviews/2026-09-23_daas_platform_review.md:221 (SPEC_137 /datasets/{key}/schema); live: pg_description column comments = 2, table comments = 39; 175 of 195 declared tables exist

recommendations.title: Make the detail page fast: fold the status snapshot in, use estimates by default, and keep exact counts behind refresh
recommendations.detail:
GET /catalog/{key} runs up to MAX_EXACT_COUNTS=12 exact count(*) calls at 5 s each under a 20 s deadline (app/catalog/live.py:34-38, 191-195), plus coverage_sql. A browsing page that makes a user wait up to 20+ s per click on sec_13f (sec_13f_holdings has about 3.8M rows by reltuples) or on sec_form_d is not usable.
For the catalog UX:
- Add `?live=estimate` (the default for the page). It uses pg_class.reltuples (estimate_rows, live.py:102-116) plus the coverage clocks and status that SPEC_124's /datasets/status already computes and caches.
- Keep exact counts on the existing admin `refresh=true` path.
- Label estimates with a tilde ('~3.8M rows'). rows_exact already carries that signal.
To populate the freshness facet, the list view should also make one call to GET /datasets/status (a user-level read) and join on key client-side, rather than N detail calls.

recommendations.title: Add a catalog-aware, rights-aware GET /catalog/{key}/sample instead of reusing the export preview
recommendations.detail:
The only row preview, /export/tables/{t}/preview (app/api/v1/export.py:195-252), is admin-only under the SPEC_127 router table. It checks only public-schema tables (inspector.get_table_names(), export.py:208), so core.entity and core.source_record can't be sampled. It runs an unbounded `SELECT COUNT(*)` (export.py:222) with no statement_timeout. And it ignores pii_class and redistribution.
New endpoint, user-level:
- up to 20 rows from tables[0], or from `?table=` restricted to resolve_tables(spec)
- `SET LOCAL statement_timeout=3000`
- ordered by the natural key or a coverage column, with no count
- mask columns tagged pii (for datasets with pii_class 'personal' or 'business_contact': 16 and 26 specs) unless the principal is admin
- 403 with an explanation when effective_redistribution is 'restricted' (25 specs)
- a response header `X-Dataset-Attribution`
Cache per key for 10 minutes. This gives the detail page a Sample tab and gives the future /data/v1 (SPEC_130) a tested masking path.
recommendations.evidence: app/api/v1/export.py:195-252 (esp. 208, 222); docs/specs/SPEC_127_access_lockdown.md router table ('export' is Admin, all methods); app/core/export_policy.py:86; live: pii personal 16, business_contact 26; redistribution restricted 25

recommendations.title: Derive related datasets from shared identifier columns, with an alias map
recommendations.detail:
Related datasets is where discovery gets most of its value, and the join keys already exist in the DB.
Live information_schema over catalog tables shows: cik in 18 tables (form_d_filings, sec_13f_filings, pe_firms, pe_funds, core.entity, core.source_record, sec_8k_index…); crd_number in 10 plus crd in 3 (core.*); naics_code in 6; county_fips in 5; zip_code in 9 plus zip in 2; ein in 4; lei in 3; cusip in 2; npi in 2; ticker in 5; state in 40.
Add app/catalog/identifiers.py:
- canonical id types mapped to column aliases, e.g. crd: {crd, crd_number}; zip: {zip, zip_code}; fips_county: {county_fips}
- `related(key)` returns the other datasets sharing each identifier, ranked by specificity (cik, crd, npi, lei, cusip ahead of naics and zip; state excluded as too generic)
Show on the detail page: 'Joins to 17 datasets on CIK', each with an example join snippet. Expose it as a `related` block on the detail response. It also doubles as a lint: alias drift like crd vs crd_number becomes visible.
recommendations.evidence: live information_schema query over the 195 catalog tables (counts in detail); app/catalog/datasets.py:245-258 (entity_master identifiers)

recommendations.title: Build lineage both ways and add a 'How to access' block per dataset
recommendations.detail:
Only 10 specs declare inputs, and the API exposes no reverse edges. registry._index validates inputs (registry.py:192-195) but builds no downstream map.
Add `downstream(key)` (datasets whose inputs include key). Render a small inline-SVG DAG on the detail page: inputs, then this dataset, then consumers. For sec_form_d, for example, this would show pe_funds_sec, pe_people_sec and entity_source_records downstream.
Add an optional `access: Tuple[AccessPath,...]` to DatasetSpec. Each path is (label, method, path, scope), e.g. entity_master maps to GET /api/v1/entity-master/by-id/{id_type}/{value} (entity_master.py:89), and export maps to POST /export/jobs (admin). Today a consumer can't tell from the catalog how to get the data. The detail page renders these with copyable curl snippets that use the X-API-Key header, and labels 'admin only' or 'not yet exposed (SPEC_130)' honestly.
recommendations.evidence: app/catalog/registry.py:179-196; app/catalog/datasets.py:208-258 (pe_marts inputs); app/api/v1/entity_master.py:58, 89; app/api/v1/pe_marts.py:55; live: inputs on 10 of 150

recommendations.title: Add data-product pages for the PE/entity pack (catalog.html#/p/pe-entity)
recommendations.detail:
Group the 7 entity and 4 pe_marts derived datasets (sec_adv_private_funds, pe_firms_sec, pe_funds_sec, pe_people_sec, entity_source_records, entity_cik_crd_bridge, entity_master) plus their SEC inputs into a declared `DataProduct` (key, name, pitch, member keys, hero identifiers, example questions, access paths) in app/catalog/products.py, served by GET /catalog/products and /catalog/products/{key}.
The page shows:
- the product story
- a member table with live freshness
- the lineage DAG from SEC bulk sources to marts to the entity master
- the identifier spine (CIK <-> CRD bridge)
- example lookups
- one rights summary, computed as the most restrictive effective_redistribution of the members, the same rule SPEC_123 uses for status_public
This is the customer-shaped entry point the DaaS review asks for, without waiting for SPEC_130.

recommendations.title: Fill metadata gaps before launch, and add a completeness score and lint
recommendations.detail:
A product page reads as empty with today's metadata:
- coverage_from on 0 of 150
- coverage_sql on 11
- primary_key on 8
- inputs on 10
- upstream_url on 8
- slo_lag_hours on 13
- notes on 6
- owner is 'data-platform' on all 150
- description median 77 chars (min 36)
- reviewed 0
Cheap wins:
(a) Auto-derive the natural key. 81 of the 85 first tables with a surrogate `id` primary key have a non-PK unique index (pg_index.indisunique), and 15 have a natural PK. Emit `natural_key` in the schema endpoint and add a test that flags drift from the declared primary_key.
(b) Add a `completeness` score per spec in to_dict(): the share of description ≥120 chars, coverage_sql, coverage_from, primary_key, upstream_url, SLO, attribution and column docs. Show it as a meter on cards and as a sortable column, so curators can see what to fill next.
(c) A test that fails when a ga/beta spec lacks the product-page minimum set.

recommendations.title: Merge the competing discovery surfaces into the catalog, or cross-link them
recommendations.detail:
Right now a user can reach:
- /sources with /{key} (sources.py:767, 829), which has its own tables and row counts
- the console Sources tab (index.html:2035, 3171)
- /metadata/datasets (metadata.py:151)
- /lineage/datasets (lineage.py:507)
- /search, which covers investors and companies only (search.py:1-20)
- /catalog
The DaaS review lists six competing catalogs (review:41). Keep each for its current job, but:

lens:dictionary.summary:
I didn't change anything in the repo. I ran SELECT-only queries against the live database (Docker was responsive the whole time) and put the measurement script in the scratchpad (cov.py). The main finding: column truth exists, but it is split across 7 places in 5 different formats, and nothing gathers it. Only 2 of the 10,089 live columns have a Postgres COMMENT. Both are the 13F value/table_value_total comments at app/ingest/bulk/sec_13f/source.py:104,109. There are 39 table comments. Across the 12 model files, 0 of 3,334 columns use Column(comment=) or doc=. 612 of them (18%) have an inline `# comment` that a parser can extract.

The other sources are:
- Hand-written description dictionaries in metadata.py for fdic (184), cms (66), nppes (30), dunl, prediction_markets, foot_traffic and bls.
- Inline `-- comments` in the DDL for realestate.
- Bulk loader column lists in three different shapes: a name list plus a type dict (13F, parse.py:246), a list of (name, type) pairs (insider, parse.py:40) and a type dict (Form D, source.py:213). None of them carries a description.
- A census_variable_metadata table (models.py:473, 196 rows) that already maps acs5 columns to labels.
- Per-column profiling stats in data_profile_columns (models.py:2537, 9,255 rows). They hold null %, distinct counts and top_values, which can supply example values.

Coverage measured on 20 datasets. That is 42 live tables and 886 columns. eia_petroleum's pattern matched no live tables.
- **Live COMMENTs:** 2 columns (0.2%).
- **Model inline comments:** 61 (6.9%).
- **metadata.py dictionaries and SQL comments:** 149 (16.8%).
- **Everything code already holds combined:** 212 (23.9%).
- **Adding census_variable_metadata:** 260 (29.3%). The acs5_2015_b01001 table goes from 1/53 to 49/53 columns.
- **Adding a 27-rule list of common column names (id, *_at, cik, crd, fips, naics, zip, lat/lon, state, name…):** 498 (56.2%).

Three datasets are close to fully covered today:
- fdic_bank_financials: 75/75
- nppes_providers: 30/30
- cms_medicare_utilization: 29/31

Seven datasets have zero columns covered by existing text: sec_adv_private_funds, entity_master, treasury_daily_balance, usaspending_awards, fred_series, osha and epa_echo_facilities. Most of what is left is concentrated in the SEC bulk tables, people_org_charts and core.* (entity_master). Those need the published field guides from upstream plus hand-written overrides. Treasury FiscalData API responses carry meta.labels and meta.dataTypes, which would cover Treasury. Adding those is projected to lift coverage to about 80%.

Findings on shared identifiers from the live database:
- **CIK:** stored as varchar in 24 columns, text in 13, integer in 7 and bigint in 3. The workbench.* schema uses integer. Public tables hold 10-digit zero-padded text (sec_filers, form_d_issuers, sec_13f_filings and pe_firms all look like '0000025743').
- **Entity master is out of step:** core.identifier stores CIK unpadded (id_type='cik' holds 123,511 rows, maximum length 7). Of 1,000 identifier CIKs, a plain join to sec_filers matched 0; with lpad(id_value,10,'0') it matched 1,000/1,000.
- **CRD:** text in 15 columns, integer in 13, varchar in 8.
- **Mislabelled PII:** 93 columns in catalog tables have names that look like personal data. For example, sec_13f has signature_name, signature_phone and filing_manager_street, yet its dataset-level pii_class is 'none'. Only a per-column PII flag can catch this.

What I recommend:
- **Where column truth lives:** keep it in code, as a generated, checked-in dictionary plus a small hand-written overrides file. Mirror it to a catalog_column table and to Postgres COMMENTs.
- **Identifiers:** tag each join column with a type from a closed list, a canonical format and a SQL expression that converts it to that format. That makes a join-keys view and a /catalog/{key}/joins endpoint possible.
- **New API:** GET /catalog/{key}/schema, and a /sample endpoint that masks PII and only returns listed columns.
- **Build order:** this fits the SPEC_137 already planned in docs/reviews/2026-09-23_daas_platform_review.md:221. Build it as the dictionary first; don't wait for the Alembic migration work.

lens:lineage-quality.summary:
Lineage/quality/ops-metadata lens. Verified in code and in the live DB with read-only SQL; Docker responded throughout.

1. **The DQ framework cannot see the flagship data.** 147 of 263 dataset_registry rows are catalog-only (last_updated_at=1970), and every DQ path filters them out through DatasetRegistry.ingested(): data_profiling_service.py:434, quality_trending_service.py:153, jobs.py:622-628. The excluded rows include every SEC bulk table (form_d_*, sec_13f_*, sec_insider_*, sec_financial_facts, sec_filers, sec_adv_*), every PE mart (pe_firms, pe_funds, pe_people, sec_adv_private_funds) and all of core.*. None of app/marts, app/entities, app/worker or the bulk loaders calls profile_table or the post-ingest hook. The SPEC_126a "DQ post-load hook on DatasetSpec.tables" has not been built.

2. **The quality numbers the framework does produce are unreliable.**
   - 107 of the 110 profiled tables were last profiled on 2026-03-11. profile_all_tables is only reachable from an API endpoint (data_quality.py:1115), with no scheduler. For example, fred_interest_rates was last profiled at 18,868 rows and now has 105,283.
   - The freshness score ignores cadence (it decays to 0 after 168h, quality_trending_service.py:57-78) and is keyed on ingestion_jobs.source, so split jobs ("eia:split_1") never match.
   - Today 22 of the 116 snapshots score 0.0.
   - The row-count-drop check compares against the snapshot the same gate just wrote (jobs.py:648, then :667; data_quality_service.py:1349-1354).
   - The profiling advisory lock uses Python hash() (data_profiling_service.py:229). Python randomizes that per process, so the lock does not protect across the api and worker processes.

3. **Lineage is not recorded anywhere, and the three declarations of mart inputs disagree.**
   - app/core/lineage_service.py (693 lines) plus the mounted /lineage router: record_job_lineage/record_job_failure have zero callers. lineage_nodes holds 2 rows and lineage_edges 1, all from a hand test on 2026-01-14. dataset_versions, lineage_events and impact_analysis are never-analysed (reltuples -1).
   - core.mart_build has 0 rows, so the mart ledger has no observed lineage yet.
   - DatasetSpec.inputs, app/marts/inputs.py PE_MART_STAGE_INPUTS and the SQL the marts actually run all differ:
     - pe_firms_sec declares sec_iapd_feed, but pe_firms_sec.py only reads sec_adv_roster_snapshots and core.identifier.
     - pe_funds_sec reads sec_adv_filings (sec_adv_schedule_d) and sec_adv_roster_snapshots. Neither is in its catalog inputs, and the mart assertion for the funds stage omits sec_adv_schedule_d.
     - pe_people_sec reads sec_adv_roster_snapshots, which is undeclared.
     - The entity bridge stage asserts sec_13f and sec_adv_roster, but the catalog says entity_source_records.

4. **A live row-count bug.** The fred_* table pattern matches the fred_observations VIEW, which is a UNION of the six fred_* tables. The fred_series live stats therefore report 132,302 rows for the view on top of the same 132,302 rows in the six base tables, doubling the total. existing_tables() includes views (live.py:50-65), and the view also got a registry row.

5. **dataset_key backfill (the 0014 column).** Only 90 of 3,809 ingestion_jobs rows have it. Running the existing job_keys.ProducerMap in memory (no writes) over the 3,719 empty rows gives:
   - 3,396 (91%) resolve to exactly one dataset.
   - 1 is ambiguous (job:pe_mart_build maps to 4 datasets).
   - 322 do not resolve: 'job_postings' 162, international_econ_oecd 24, census_bfs 14, usda 10, worldbank 9, and form_d/form_adv/app_rankings/web_traffic/opencorporates/epa_echo about 7 each. These are missing dispatch aliases.

6. **Usage metadata does not exist.** A static FROM/JOIN scan of app/api/v1, services, graphql and reports finds no SQL reader for 86 of 150 specs. The scan is a heuristic: it misses views and dynamic table names. Two real paths it cannot see:

lens:rights.summary:
I compared every source family in app/catalog/rights.py (SOURCE_RIGHTS, COLLECTOR_RIGHTS, DATASET_RIGHTS), covering the 150 specs grouped by source and collector, against the official terms pages. I also checked the live DB (read-only; Docker responded) to see which restricted sources actually hold rows.

**Wrong or unsafe today:**
1. **HIFLD** (collector `hifld`) falls through to the site_intel family default `open` (rights.py:146-148). DHS removed the substation layer from public release in 2022 and shut down HIFLD Open on 2025-08-26. The collector now pulls 8,738 substations from a Rutgers ArcGIS mirror (hifld_collector.py:51-52) and also holds 52,244 transmission lines.
2. **CMS Medicare utilization** (rights.py:211) is marked `_usg` (US Government work) and `open`. All 21,260 rows carry `hcpcs_cd`/`hcpcs_desc` with CPT Level I codes, which are AMA copyright. CMS shows its AMA CPT licence agreement before access.
3. **BIS and IMF** are marked `attribution`, but both have commercial conditions:
   - BIS statistics may not add a charge to subscribers.
   - IMF says to email copyright@imf.org for commercial reuse, and anyone selling IMF Data as a standalone product must tell buyers it is free.
4. **CourtListener** is marked `attribution`. The court records are public domain, but the API's terms route product or team use to a commercial agreement.
5. **The site_intel family default** gives 27 collectors a license string of "Mixed..." and no attribution. NREL-run sources (AFDC, `nrel_resource`) are contractor works, not strictly 17 U.S.C. §105.

**Correctly `restricted`, but the enum can't say storage itself breaks the terms.** These are stored in the DB today:
- Yelp: 400 rows. The terms allow caching for at most 24 hours and ban building your own database.
- FRED: about 131k rows. The terms ban caching and archiving the FRED Services.
- Kaggle M5: 30k items. The data is licensed for non-commercial use only.
- Kalshi prediction markets: 25 rows. The terms ban providing archived data sets to others.
- National Zoning Atlas: 3,695 rows. The terms ban hosting and storing without written permission.
- PeeringDB: 216 rows. The terms ban "any other commercial application".
- LoopNet: 60 scraped rows. The terms ban scraping and building a database.

**FRED is fixable.** 23 of the 24 stored series are public-domain data from BLS, BEA, the Federal Reserve Board, EIA and Census, so they can be sourced from those agencies directly and marked `open`. Only UMCSENT is copyrighted (University of Michigan).

**Good Jobs First provenance is unknown.** The `incentive_deal` table has 48 rows with source='gjf_expanded', but the collector's data path was removed (PLAN_082). `origin='scraped'` is wrong.

**Over-restrictive:** OSM is licensed under ODbL, which allows commercial redistribution with attribution and share-alike. It needs a `share_alike` flag rather than `restricted`.

**Candidates for reviewed=true** (a human still has to sign off):
- US federal statistical families: treasury, bls, bea, eia, census, us_trade, bts, cftc_cot, usda, fdic, fema (with the OpenFEMA notice), irs_soi, fbi_crime, osha, epa_echo, usaspending
- fda: CC0
- Non-PII SEC datasets: sec_13f, sec_companyfacts, sec_company_financials
- fcc_broadband: Form 477/BDC aggregates, which contain no Fabric locations
- realestate_fhfa_hpi and realestate_hud_permits
- intl_worldbank and intl_oecd: CC BY 4.0
- uspto (PatentsView): CC BY 4.0
- epoch_dc: CC BY 4.0
- openei_urdb: CC0
- The USGS, EPA, BTS, FRA, USACE, FWS and DOT site_intel collectors, once they get their own entries

PII-bearing public-domain datasets need a separate PII-policy decision: nppes, sec_insider, sec_form_d, sec_edgar_submissions, sam_gov and pe_people_sec.

**Not verified directly** (the page blocked the fetch or had no text, so these rest on search excerpts):
- IMF and BIS full terms pages returned 403.
- DUNL's licence page didn't render.
- The GJF plans page returned 403.
- Drewry and SCFI publish no terms page.
- NREL's developer terms failed with a DNS error.
- The FDIC and NASS terms pages were not fetched.

I made no repo edits and ran only SELECT queries and pg_class estimates.

- FRED: no 'caching, or archiving any portion of the FRED Services'.

- Kalshi: no 'archived or cached data sets'.

Add SourceRights.storage in {'permitted','ttl_24h','forbidden'} or a commercial_use flag. Surface it on /catalog, then purge the data or get written licences. Medspa/vertical prospects inherit the Yelp problem.

recommendations.detail:
Attribution values currently hold only 'Source: X'. Several sources require specific text:
- FRED: 'This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis'.
- OpenFEMA: 'This product uses the FEMA OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA...', plus dataset name and version.
- Census API: its non-endorsement line.
- OECD, on adaptations: 'This is an adaptation of an original work by the OECD'.
- Epoch: citation 'Epoch AI, AI Data Centers'.
- OSM: '© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL'.
- Freightos: credit plus a link to terminal.freightos.com.

recommendations.title: Model share-alike (OSM, OpenCorporates) instead of lumping it into 'restricted'
recommendations.detail: The ODbL allows commercial copying and distribution with attribution. Only derived databases must stay under ODbL. realestate_osm_buildings (rights.py:193) could be 'attribution' with share_alike=True, served as a separate layer and not merged into proprietary tables. OpenCorporates free keys are share-alike only; the non-share-alike rights require a paid key, so it stays restricted unless a paid key is used.

recommendations.title: Resolve the low-confidence entries: DUNL, Redfin, NOAA non-US, SAM.gov key level, Tranco
recommendations.detail:
- DUNL: S&P describes it as Creative Commons-licensed open data. Confirm the exact CC variant; it may be downgradable from restricted.
- Redfin: the Data Center asks for a citation and link, but I found no explicit resale grant. Keep restricted and ask for written permission.
- NOAA GHCND: WMO Resolution 40 means non-U.S. station data 'shall not be provided to other users or be used for the re-export of commercial services'. Add a note (no NOAA tables are loaded today).
- SAM.gov: confirm the key is public-sensitivity only, because the FOUO/sensitive tiers ban dissemination.
- Tranco: the list includes Cloudflare Radar (CC BY-NC), so keep restricted.
